# Getting Started

This guide will walk you through the steps to quickly set up and test our API. You have two main options for testing:

- **Native Documentation Interface**: Use the built-in testing interface directly in your browser
- **External Tools**: Use tools like [Postman](https://www.postman.com/) or [Insomnia](https://insomnia.rest/)

Choose the method that best fits your workflow and testing needs.

---

## Testing with Native Documentation Interface

The documentation interface provides a built-in testing environment directly in the API documentation. This is the quickest way to test endpoints.

### 1. Navigate to an API Endpoint

- Browse through the API documentation to find the endpoint you want to test
- Click on the endpoint to expand its details

---

### 2. Access the Test Interface

- On the right side of the endpoint documentation, you'll find a code snippet box showing example requests
- Click the **"Test Request"** button to open the interactive testing interface

---

### 3. Configure Variables

- In the testing interface, locate the **"Variables"** section
- Fill in all required variables for the endpoint you're testing
- These variables typically include path parameters, query parameters, and request body data

---

### 4. Set Up Authentication

- Navigate to the **"Headers"** section in the test interface
- Add a new header with:
  - **Key**: `Authorization`
  - **Value**: `Bearer YOUR_TOKEN_HERE` (keep the literal prefix `Bearer` followed by a single space, and replace `YOUR_TOKEN_HERE` with your actual token)

> **Important:**
>
> - Token generation must be implemented in your local code using your specific authentication flow. Refer to the Authentication section for detailed implementation guidance.
> - Tokens have expiration times. If you receive authentication errors, verify that your token is still valid and generate a new one if necessary.

**Alternative — API Key:** If you have a static API Key, add the header `x-api-key: YOUR_API_KEY` instead of the `Authorization` header. No token generation is required. Refer to the Authentication section for details on obtaining an API Key.

---

### 5. Execute the Request

- Review all configured variables and headers
- Click **"Send Request"** to execute the API call
- View the response directly in the interface

---

## Testing with Postman

For other testing scenarios, you can use Postman to create comprehensive test suites and manage multiple environments.

### 1. Install Postman

Download and install the [Postman](https://www.postman.com/) application on your machine.

---

### 2. Import the API Specification

Import the OpenAPI specification to access all endpoints directly in Postman:

- Open **Postman** and click on **Import** in the top-left corner
- In the dialog, select the **Link** tab and enter: [https://api.dynamox.solutions/openapi.json](https://api.dynamox.solutions/openapi.json)
- Click **Import** and finish the import

Alternatively, you can download the file first by visiting the [URL](https://api.dynamox.solutions/openapi.json) above and saving it with **Ctrl + S** as a `.json` file, or by clicking the **"Download OpenAPI Document"** button at the top of this page, then import the downloaded file in Postman.

You should now see a new collection named **Dynamox API**.

---

### 3. Set Up Environment Variables

Create a Postman environment to manage your API configuration:

- Select the **Dynamox API** collection root
- Go to the **Variables** tab
- Add the following variable:

**Variable Name**: `baseUrl`  
**Initial Value**: `https://api.dynamox.solutions/v1`  
**Current Value**: `https://api.dynamox.solutions/v1`

---

### 4. Configure Authentication

Set up the collection to use Bearer Token authentication:

- Select the **Dynamox API** collection root
- Go to the **Auth** tab
- In the **Auth Type** dropdown, select **Bearer Token**
- In the **Token** field, enter your generated Bearer token

> **Important:**
>
> - Token generation must be implemented in your local code using your specific authentication flow. Refer to the Authentication section for detailed implementation guidance.
> - Tokens have expiration times. If you receive authentication errors, verify that your token is still valid and generate a new one if necessary.

**Alternative — API Key:**

If you have a static API Key, skip the **Auth** tab configuration and instead add the key directly in the **Headers** tab:

- Go to the **Headers** tab
- Add a new header with:
  - **Key**: `x-api-key`
  - **Value**: `dyp_YOUR_API_KEY_HERE`

Example cURL:

```bash
curl -X GET "https://api.dynamox.solutions/v1/<endpoint>" \
  -H "x-api-key: dyp_YOUR_API_KEY_HERE"
```

---

### 5. Test Your Configuration

Verify everything is set up correctly:

- Expand the **Dynamox API** collection
- Navigate to any endpoint group
- Select a request from the available endpoints
- Ensure the request URL uses the variables correctly
- Click **Send**

If configured properly, you should receive a successful response from the API.

---

# Endpoints Interactions Map

The **Endpoints Interactions Map** provides a high-level overview of how the available endpoints relate to each other within the API.  
Its purpose is to help developers and integrators clearly understand the logical flow of data, from authentication to resource consumption and management.

## Map Image

![Endpoints Interactions Map](/assets/endpoint.interaction.map.png)

This visual guide is designed to:

- Show the sequence of calls required to access different resources.
- Clarify dependencies between endpoints.
- Simplify navigation through the API by highlighting the main entry points and their possible paths.
- Provide a reference that reduces trial-and-error during integration.

By following the interactions map, clients can quickly identify **where to start**, **what steps are required**, and **how to reach the desired endpoints** in an efficient and structured way.

---

# Rate Limit

Our API follows the rate-limit standard defined in [draft-ietf-httpapi-ratelimit-headers-08](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-ietf-httpapi-ratelimit-headers/).

---

## Rate Limit Windows

The rate-limit system operates with three distinct time windows:

- **Per Minute**: Maximum number of requests allowed per minute
- **Per Hour**: Maximum number of requests allowed per hour
- **Per Day**: Maximum number of requests allowed per day

These limits are proportionally calculated based on your contract's daily quota:

- **Minute limit**: Daily quota / 10
- **Hour limit**: Daily quota / 4
- **Day limit**: Daily quota (as defined in your contract)

**Example**: If your daily quota is 500 requests → 50/minute, 125/hour, 500/day.

---

## Sliding Window Concept

Our rate limiting uses a **sliding window** approach, not calendar-based periods:

- **"Per Day" means the last 24 hours** from the current moment, not midnight to midnight
- **"Per Hour" means the last 60 minutes** from the current moment
- **"Per Minute" means the last 60 seconds** from the current moment

#### Practical Example

If you reach your daily limit of 500 requests at 6:00 PM today, all requests made between 6:00 PM yesterday and 6:00 PM today count toward this limit. You can only make new requests as older requests "expire" from the 24-hour window.

**Key Points**:

- Limits don't reset at midnight
- New request capacity becomes available as old requests age out of their respective windows
- The system continuously tracks usage across rolling time periods

---

## Blocking Rules

The system evaluates all three windows for every request:

- **Check all windows**: Minute, hour, and daily usage are compared against their respective limits
- **Block on any exceeded limit**: If **any** window exceeds its limit, the request is blocked with a `429 Too Many Requests` error
- **Dynamic availability**: Request capacity becomes available as older requests expire from their time windows

---

## Rate Limit Response Headers

All API responses include the following headers to help track rate limit usage:

- **RateLimit-Policy**: Defines the quota policies, indicating the maximum number of allowed requests (`q`) and the window duration (`w`).
- **RateLimit**: Indicates the actual available request rate (`r`) and the remaining time for renewal (`t`) for each policy.

Both headers also include the parameter `pk`, which identifies the application or contract associated with each quota entry.

---

## Example Response with Rate Limit

```http
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json
RateLimit-Policy: "minutely";pk=:NjdhOWY:;q=100;w=60,"hourly";pk=:NjdhOWY:;q=500;w=3600,"daily";pk=:NjdhOWY:;q=1000;w=86400
RateLimit: "minutely";pk=:NjdhOWY:;t=30;r=50,"hourly";pk=:NjdhOWY:;t=1350;r=300,"daily";pk=:NjdhOWY:;t=1350;r=100

{
  "message": "Request successful"
}
```

---

## Exceeding the Limit

If you exceeds the allowed quota, the API will return a [429 Too Many Requests](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTTP/Status/429) error, with a [Retry-After](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/Retry-After) header indicating the time in seconds until a new request is allowed.

```http
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
RateLimit-Policy: "minutely";pk=:NjdhOWY:;q=100;w=60,"hourly";pk=:NjdhOWY:;q=500;w=3600,"daily";pk=:NjdhOWY:;q=1000;w=86400
RateLimit: "minutely";pk=:NjdhOWY:;t=30;r=0,"hourly";pk=:NjdhOWY:;t=1350;r=300,"daily";pk=:NjdhOWY:;t=1350;r=100
Retry-After: 30

{
  "error": "Request limit exceeded. Please try again in 30 seconds."
}
```

---

# Authentication

The API supports two authentication methods. Use the one that best fits your integration:

| Method | Header | Best for |
|---|---|---|
| **Bearer Token** (JWT RS256) | `Authorization: Bearer <token>` | Programmatic integrations that allow generation, refresh and management of JWT tokens |
| **Static API Key** | `x-api-key: <key>` | Integrations to software platforms that do not support dynamic token generation |

Both methods grant the same level of access.

---

## Bearer Token

The Bearer Token method requires exchanging a signed JWT (RS256) for a short-lived access token via the Token endpoint. The JWT must be signed with your Application Key's private key.

Refer to the **Token** section in the API documentation for the full step-by-step, code examples (Python, Node.js, cURL), and common errors.

---

## API Key

A static API Key is an opaque credential linked to a specific Application. Key characteristics:

- **Generated once, never recoverable**: the full key value is shown only at creation time — store it securely immediately.
- **Format**: keys always start with the prefix `dyp_` (e.g. `dyp_Abc123...`).
- **Limit**: up to 25 active keys per Application.
- **Expiration**: configurable at creation; maximum (and default) is 365 days. A key can be in one of three states: `ACTIVE`, `EXPIRED`, or `REVOKED`. Keys are automatically set to `EXPIRED` when the expiration date is reached.
- **Revocation**: keys can be manually revoked at any time through Dynamox web platform, by setting their state to `REVOKED`.

### How to obtain an API Key

API Keys are managed through the Dynamox Platform. To create one, navigate to:

**Connectors → API Dynamox → Select Contract → Select Application → Create Key**

> **Important:** You need administrator permissions to create/manage API Keys.
> **Important:** Copy and store the full key (`dyp_...`) immediately after creation. It will not be displayed again.

### Using the key in requests

Include the key in every request via the `x-api-key` header:

```http
GET /v1/<endpoint> HTTP/1.1
Host: api.dynamox.solutions
x-api-key: dyp_YOUR_API_KEY_HERE
```

import json
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from time import sleep

import jwt  # pip install pyjwt
import requests  # pip install requests

TOKEN_URL = "https://api.dynamox.solutions/v1/token"

APPLICATION_KEY_PATH = "your_key.json"

def generate_jwt(application_key_path: str) -> str:
    with open(application_key_path) as file:
        key = json.load(file)

    return jwt.encode(
      headers={
        "kid": key["_id"],
        "alg": "RS256",
        "typ": "JWT",
      },
      payload={
        "iat": datetime.now(timezone.utc).timestamp(),
        "email": key["email"],
      },
      key=key["privateKey"].encode("utf-8"),
    )

def main() -> None:
    encoded_jwt = generate_jwt(APPLICATION_KEY_PATH)
    sleep(2)
    response = requests.post(
        url=TOKEN_URL,
        headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {encoded_jwt}"},
        timeout=10,
    )
    print(response.json())
    access_token = response.json().get("access_token")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

get.description:
### Get Alert History

Retrieve an alert history by its `policyId`.

The `fromTime` and `toTime` parameters are optional and allow you to filter the alert history by a specific time range.

Returns a list of alert history objects, including:
- Timestamp, alert policy ID and alert status.

> **Note:** The `fromTime` and `toTime` parameters must be in the format "YYYY-MM-DD" (e.g. `2022-01-01`) or "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS" (e.g. `2022-01-01T00:00:00`).

> **Note:** If `fromTime` is not provided, the default value is the current time minus 7 days. If `toTime` is not provided, the default value is the current time.

> **Note:** The data is only available for the past 7 days from the current date. If a date earlier than 7 days is provided, we will set the `fromTime` to 7 days before the current date.

> **Note:** If the `fromTime` is greater than the `toTime`, the request will not return any alert history.

### Returns a paginated list of tags for a specific workspace

This endpoint provides access to all tags that have been mapped and configured for data integration with the Dynamox platform. It supports advanced filtering, searching, and sorting capabilities to help you efficiently navigate through large TAG datasets.

**Key Features:**
- Pagination support for handling large TAG lists
- Status-based filtering (connected, disconnected, etc.)
- Partial name search with case-insensitive matching
- Flexible sorting by tag, status, or last sync time

**Usage Tips:**
- Use the `status` filter to find TAGs in specific states
- Combine `search` with `status` for precise TAG discovery
- Adjust `limit` based on your application's pagination needs

### Receives and processes telemetry data for a specific tag

This endpoint allows sending telemetry data points collected from the client's tag to the Dynamox platform. Data is processed asynchronously and integrated into monitoring and analysis systems.

**Features:**
- Asynchronous processing of received data
- Automatic data quality validation
- Support for multiple data points in a single request
- Preservation of tag quality flags

**Processing Flow:**
1. Tag validation and workspace permissions
2. Data structure and quality verification
3. Queuing for asynchronous processing
4. Integration with Dynamox analysis systems

⚠️ **Requirements:**
- Timestamps must be in ISO 8601 format

💡 **Tip:** Use the GET endpoint to check if the tag is available before sending data.

post.description:
Creates a new Configuration Slot in the Digitalization Platform.

Configuration Slots define how Measuring Systems monitor specific locations within your assets. They establish the relationship between a Measuring System Model, monitoring locations, and the configuration parameters needed for data collection.

## Key Concepts

**Configuration Slot**: A template that defines monitoring parameters for a specific Measuring System Model. It can be associated with a Measuring System to enable data collection from monitored resources.

**Measuring System Model**: Defines the capabilities and requirements of measuring devices. Each Configuration Slot must reference a valid Measuring System Model by name and version.

**Monitoring Location Map**: Maps logical monitoring points (like "bearing1", "motor") to actual monitored resource IDs in your asset hierarchy.

**Configuration**: Device-specific parameters that control how measurements are taken (sampling rates, filters, etc.).

**Measuring System Unique Identifier**: Optional field that can be set to `null` or contain the identifier of an existing Measuring System resource. This can be either a 24-character hexadecimal ID or a custom string identifier that was registered when creating the Measuring System via the POST measuring-systems endpoint. When `null`, the Configuration Slot is created as a template without active monitoring. When specified with a valid identifier, the Configuration Slot is immediately associated and ready for data collection.

## Required Information

Before creating a Configuration Slot, ensure you have:
- A valid Measuring System Model (name and version)
- Parent resource ID (the asset or component being monitored)
- Monitoring location mappings
- Configuration parameters matching the model's schema
- (Optional) Measuring System Unique Identifier if you want immediate association

## Usage Flow

You have two options when creating a Configuration Slot:

**Option 1: Create with immediate association**
1. Create Configuration Slot with `measuringSystemUniqueIdentifier` specified (this endpoint)
2. Start collecting telemetry data through the telemetry cycles endpoint

**Option 2: Create and associate later**
1. Create Configuration Slot with `measuringSystemUniqueIdentifier` set to `null` (this endpoint)
2. Associate with a Measuring System using the association endpoint when ready
3. Start collecting telemetry data through the telemetry cycles endpoint

Both approaches are valid - choose based on whether you have the Measuring System ready at creation time or prefer to set up the configuration template first and associate it later.

## Validation

The system validates:
- Measuring System Model exists and is accessible
- Parent resource exists and is accessible
- Configuration matches the model's configuration schema
- Monitoring locations reference valid resources
- User has appropriate permissions

patch.description:
Associates an existing Configuration Slot with a Measuring System in the Digitalization Platform.

This endpoint enables you to link a previously created Configuration Slot template with an active Measuring System, establishing the connection required for data collection and monitoring.

## Key Concepts

**Configuration Slot Association**: The process of connecting a Configuration Slot template to a specific Measuring System resource. Once associated, the Measuring System can begin collecting telemetry data from the monitored locations defined in the Configuration Slot.

**Measuring System Unique Identifier**: The identifier of the Measuring System resource you want to associate. This corresponds to the string identifier that was registered when creating the Measuring System via the POST measuring-systems endpoint.

**Configuration Slot**: A template that defines monitoring parameters for a specific Measuring System Model, including the monitoring location mappings and configuration parameters needed for data collection.

## When to Use This Endpoint

Use this endpoint when:
- You created a Configuration Slot with `measuringSystemUniqueIdentifier` set to `null` and now want to activate it
- You need to associate an existing Configuration Slot template with a new or different Measuring System
- You want to enable data collection for a Configuration Slot that was previously created without immediate association

## Required Information

Before associating a Configuration Slot, ensure you have:
- The Configuration Slot ID of the slot you want to associate
- A valid Measuring System Unique Identifier
- Confirmation that the Measuring System Model matches the Configuration Slot requirements
- Appropriate permissions to access both the Configuration Slot and the Measuring System

## Usage Flow

The typical workflow for using this endpoint:

1. Create a Configuration Slot with `measuringSystemUniqueIdentifier` set to `null` (if not already created)
2. Create or identify the Measuring System resource you want to monitor with
3. Associate the Configuration Slot with the Measuring System using this endpoint
4. Start collecting telemetry data through the telemetry cycles endpoint

This approach provides flexibility by allowing you to set up monitoring templates first and activate them when ready.

## Validation

The system validates:
- Configuration Slot exists and is accessible
- Measuring System exists and is accessible via the provided identifier
- Measuring System Model is compatible with the Configuration Slot requirements
- All monitored resources referenced in the Configuration Slot monitoring location map are accessible
- No conflicting Configuration Slot association already exists for the same resources
- User has appropriate permissions for both resources

## Important Notes

- Once associated, the Configuration Slot becomes active and ready for data collection
- The association creates a binding between the Measuring System and the monitored resources defined in the Configuration Slot
- If the Configuration Slot was already associated with another Measuring System, the association will be updated (if permitted)
- The Measuring System Model must match the requirements defined in the Configuration Slot

patch.summary: Disassociate a measuring system from a ConfigurationSlot
patch.description:
Disassociates one or more Configuration Slots from their associated Measuring Systems in the Digitalization Platform.

This endpoint enables you to break the link between Configuration Slot templates and their active Measuring Systems, effectively stopping data collection and monitoring for the specified slots.

## Key Concepts

**Configuration Slot Disassociation**: The process of removing the connection between Configuration Slot templates and their associated Measuring Systems. Once disassociated, the Configuration Slot returns to an inactive state and can be associated with the same or a different Measuring System later.

**Batch Operation**: This endpoint supports disassociating multiple Configuration Slots in a single request, allowing efficient management when you need to deactivate monitoring for several slots simultaneously.

**Configuration Slot State**: After disassociation, the Configuration Slot template is preserved with all its monitoring parameters and configuration, but its `measuringSystemUniqueIdentifier` is set back to `null`, indicating it is no longer actively monitoring.

## When to Use This Endpoint

Use this endpoint when:
- You need to temporarily stop monitoring for one or more Configuration Slots
- A Measuring System is being decommissioned or replaced
- You want to reconfigure a Configuration Slot before associating it
- You need to free up a Configuration Slot to associate it with a different Measuring System
- You are performing maintenance and need to pause data collection

## Required Information

Before disassociating Configuration Slots, ensure you have:
- The Configuration Slot IDs of the slots you want to disassociate
- Confirmation that stopping data collection for these slots is intended
- Appropriate permissions to modify the Configuration Slots
- Understanding of the impact on ongoing monitoring and data collection

## Usage Flow

The typical workflow for using this endpoint:

1. Identify the Configuration Slot(s) that need to be disassociated
2. Call this endpoint with the array of Configuration Slot IDs
3. The system breaks the association with their respective Measuring Systems
4. Configuration Slots return to an inactive state and can be associated later if needed
5. Data collection stops for the disassociated slots

This approach provides flexibility by allowing you to deactivate monitoring templates while preserving their configuration for future use.

## Validation

The system validates:
- All provided Configuration Slot IDs exist and are accessible
- Configuration Slots are currently associated with Measuring Systems
- User has appropriate permissions to modify all specified Configuration Slots
- No active telemetry cycles are in progress that would be disrupted
- All Configuration Slot IDs follow the correct format (24-character hexadecimal)

## Important Notes

- Once disassociated, data collection immediately stops for the affected Configuration Slots
- The Configuration Slot template and its monitoring parameters are preserved and can be associated later
- Historical telemetry data collected before disassociation remains available
- You can disassociate multiple Configuration Slots in a single request for efficiency
- After disassociation, the Configuration Slot can be associated with the same or a different Measuring System
- This operation does not delete the Configuration Slot; use the DELETE endpoint if removal is needed

post.description:
Telemetry Cycles are the mechanism through which Measuring Systems send data to Monitoring Locations in the Digitalization Platform. This guide explains how to create a Telemetry Cycle that follows the rules established by your Measuring System's Model.

## Objective

This documentation teaches you how to create and send a Telemetry Cycle in the Dynamox Digitalization Platform, ensuring telemetry data is correctly associated with Monitoring Locations. You'll learn how to retrieve necessary information about the Measuring System, Configuration Slot, and Models, and how to structure the request body according to defined schemas.

## Steps to Create a Telemetry Cycle

### 1. Retrieve Required Information

1.1 **Identify the Measuring System Resource** - Determine which Measuring System Resource will send the data and retrieve its `_id`.

1.2 **Get the Associated Configuration Slot** - Retrieve the Configuration Slot associated with your Measuring System using:
   `GET https://predict.dynamox.solutions/psa/v1alpha/configuration-slots?workspaceId={your-workspace-id}&measuringSystemId={your-measuring-system-id}`
   
   Save these values:
   - `measuringSystemModel.name`
   - `measuringSystemModel.version`
   - `measuringSystemId`
   - `monitoringLocationMap` entries
   - `configuration`

1.3 **Get Resource Model Information** - Retrieve the Model referenced by the Configuration Slot:
   `GET https://predict.dynamox.solutions/psa/v1/resource-models?workspaceId={your-workspace-id}&name={model-name}&version={model-version}`
   
   Save:
   - `metadata.configurationSchema`
   - `metadata.telemetryCycleSchema`

### 2. Create the Request Body

Structure your request with:
- `telemetryCycleData.measuringSystemId`: The Measuring System ID
- `telemetryCycleData.tags`: Relevant tags for the cycle
- `telemetryCycleData.measurements`: Array of measurement objects containing:
  - `resourceId`: The Monitoring Location ID from `monitoringLocationMap`
  - `attributes`: Object following the schema in `metadata.telemetryCycleSchema.attributes`
  - `dataPoints`: Array of objects with `timestamp` and `value` pairs
- `telemetryCycleData.metadata`: Object following the schema in `metadata.telemetryCycleSchema.metadata`
- `workspaceId`: Your workspace ID
- `configuration`: Object following the schema in `metadata.configurationSchema`

### 3. Send the Request and Verify

Send a POST request to `https://predict.dynamox.solutions/psa/v1/telemetry-cycles` with your structured body.

### 4. Verify Data Visualization

Access the Dynamox Solution and navigate to the Spot Viewer for the relevant Monitoring Locations to confirm your data appears in the graphs.

Alert Policies
tags.description:
This API allows you to **retrieve a single alert policy** or **list all alert policies** associated with a resource (spot) or **get alert history** by policy id. Alert policies define the rules and thresholds for generating alerts based on telemetry or spectral metrics.

### Supported Policy Types
- `telemetry`: For alerts based on telemetry metrics (requires a metric descriptor ID).
- `spectralMetrics`: For alerts based on spectral metrics (uses axis, physical quantity, processing, and frequency range).

### Possible Status Values
The `currentStatus` field can have the following values:
- `no-alert`: The policy has not been alarmed.
- `a1`: The policy has been alarmed at level A1.
- `a2`: The policy has been alarmed at level A2.

tags.name: Waveform
tags.description:
This API provides access to waveform data and related metrics. Users can retrieve raw waveforms (time-domain), spectra (frequency-domain), and computed scalar metrics derived from the waveforms or their spectral analysis. 

### Key concepts

- **Waveform**: A waveform is a time series of data points, collected by a sensor with a high sampling rate.
- **Spectrum**: The spectrum is a representation of the waveform in the frequency domain. It is uniquely identified by its `waveformId`.
- **Spectral metrics**: These are metrics computed based on the waveform and its spectrum. They are very useful for monitoring the health of rotating machinery and can be interpreted for identifying failure modes. Each spectral metric has attributes such as `physicalQuantity` (e.g. `acceleration`, `velocity`, `displacement`), `statisticalProcessing` (e.g. `rms`, `crest`, `kurtosis`), and `band` (e.g. `global`, `100-200`, `2000-6200`).

tags.name: DynaDetect
tags.description:
This API provides access to automatic fault detection by Dynamox's AI engine. Each waveform measured from a supported asset is analyzed and an automatic fault detection diagnosis is provided.

Each fault can have one of the following statuses:

- `detected`: The fault was evaluated and detected.
- `notEvaluated`: The configuration of the monitoring point does not contain the necessary information to evaluate the fault or the measured waveform is not suitable for analysis.
- `notDetected`: The fault was evaluated and was **not** detected.

tags.name: Checklist Answers
tags.description:
Checklist Answers represent the completed inspection forms submitted by inspectors during route execution. They capture the state and condition of equipment at a specific point in time. Key features include:

- **Inspection Data**: Records when (answeredAt), where (latitude/longitude), and by whom (inspectorId) the inspection was performed
- **Alert Classification**: Categorizes findings by severity level (levelAlert) to highlight critical issues
- **Attachments**: Supports documentation with images, audio recordings, and other files
- **Justifications**: Allows for explanations when inspections cannot be completed as planned
- **Geolocation**: Records the physical location where the inspection was performed
- **Synchronization**: Supports offline data collection with subsequent synchronization

Checklist Answers provide the foundation for condition monitoring, enabling trend analysis and predictive maintenance strategies based on historical inspection data.

tags.name: Cycles
tags.description:
Cycles represent execution instances of a route in a specific period. They are automatically created based on the route's periodicity configuration and control the inspection flow. Key features include:

- **Execution Period**: Defined by cycleStartAt and cycleEndAt, determining the valid time window for performing inspections
- **Status**: Can be open (opened=true) or closed (opened=false), indicating whether they still accept inspections
- **Inspector**: User designated as responsible for performing inspections in that cycle
- **Adherence Metrics**: Calculation of adherence and adherenceReal based on the proportion of inspections performed vs. scheduled
- **Counters**: Tracking of checklists, spots, machines, subsets, and components inspected
- **Justifications**: Possibility to justify cycles not fully completed
- **Alerts**: Classification of alerts (a1, a2, noAlert) based on inspection responses

 Cycles are essential for monitoring route execution over time, allowing trend analysis and identification of recurring equipment problems.

tags.name: Inspectors
tags.description:
Inspectors are users responsible for executing route inspections in the field. They interact directly with equipment and record observations through the system.

Inspectors serve as the critical human element in the condition monitoring process, providing expert assessment and documentation of equipment status during route execution.

tags.name: Route Items
tags.description:
Route Items represent the hierarchical structure of assets within a route that need to be inspected. They organize inspection points in a logical structure. Key features include:

- **Hierarchical Organization**: Structured in three levels - machines, subsets, and components
- **Asset Identification**: Each item has a unique externalId linking to the physical asset
- **Inspection Requirements**: Items may have associated checklists, quizzes, or spectral analysis requirements
- **Sorting Order**: Items can be arranged in a specific sequence for optimal inspection flow
- **Custom Periodicity**: Individual items can have multipliers that adjust their inspection frequency
- **Parent-Child Relationships**: Items maintain references to their parent items, creating a tree structure
- **Type Classification**: Items are categorized by type (machine, subset, component) for filtering and reporting

Route Items provide the structural framework for organizing inspections, ensuring comprehensive coverage of all equipment parts that require monitoring.

tags.name: Routes
tags.description:
Routes are configurable inspection plans that define a set of items (machines, subsets, components) and checklists to be inspected with a specific frequency. Each route has a lifecycle that includes creation, activation, inspection execution, and possible deactivation. Key features include:

- **Versioning**: Routes maintain a version history when significant changes are made, especially when there are existing associated responses
- **Periodicity**: Defined by frequency and frequencyUnit (hours, days, months, years)
- **Tolerance**: Configurable periods before (toleranceBefore) and after (toleranceAfter) the ideal deadline for inspection
- **Asset Hierarchy**: Organization into machines, subsets, and components through route items
- **Checklists and Spots**: Inspection points associated with route items
- **Cycles**: Execution instances of the route in specific periods
- **Responsibilities**: Users can be designated as responsible for executing inspections
- **Categorization**: Routes can be organized into categories for better management

Routes are the foundation for predictive and preventive maintenance planning, allowing systematic monitoring of equipment condition.

tags.name: Asset Pro
tags.description:
This API provides specialist metrics for assets.

## Vibrating screen

There are important concepts for the Asset Pro's vibrating screen endpoints. Users can retrieve metrics or orbits from a given metric group. First they shall request the metric group ids with the vibrating screen id. Users may request metrics and orbits with the metric group id.

- **Metric group**: A metric group is a grouping of the 4 evaluated measurement events (feed-right, feed-left, discharge-right, discharge-left) at a give time range. It is uniquely identified by its `metricGroupId`.

- **Metrics**: The specialized metrics calculated. They can be either from a spot (e.g. `stroke`, `angle`, `gForce`, `rpm`, `maxAcceleration`, `maxDisplacement`) or from the machine  (e.g. `diagonalAngle`, `rpm` or comparison of spot metrics relative to feed-discharge or right-left references).

- **Orbits**: The orbits are the processed waveforms that, when plotted, resemble the vibrating screen movement.
